infrared.def: Infrared radiation (IR): invisible radiation with longer wavelengths than visible light, given off by warm objects such as Earth’s surface. Greenhouse gases absorb it.

greenhouse-gas.def: A gas that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation, warming the lower atmosphere: water vapor, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs and HFCs (GHGs).

greenhouse-effect.def: The warming of Earth’s surface and lower atmosphere because greenhouse gases absorb infrared from the surface and re-emit part of it downward. The natural effect keeps Earth about 33 °C warmer; added gases strengthen it.

gwp.def: Global warming potential (GWP): how much heat a mass of a gas traps over a set time, usually 100 years, compared with the same mass of carbon dioxide (GWP 1). Mass × GWP gives the CO₂ equivalent.

nitrous-oxide.def: Nitrous oxide (N₂O): a greenhouse gas that traps roughly 265 to 300 times as much heat as the same mass of CO₂ over 100 years (the IPCC value depends on the report), released mostly by fertilized soils, manure and burning fuel. It lasts over a century in the air.
